_help: (design §GO.11, queue 125, Claude Code) The oracle's library: the sacred texts, a collection to read, not a puzzle. Each text: title, keeper (who holds it in the realms: an anonymous figure unless `depict` says otherwise; §GO.11.5: no religious figure is depicted unless the data says so, and the Quran's keeper is never a depiction of Muhammad), realm_area (crawler.json areas key whose oracle holds it; null: not placed yet, §GO.11 open: which realm holds which text), source (the translation to quote, §GO.11.4: respected public-domain translations, never remixed), pages (the text as pages; placeholders until Mike fills them). Read at the hub: the read-tome key opens your library (left and right turn the pages, Esc closes).

_help_iching: The I Ching cast at the fire (§GO.11.2): sit on a log by the hub fire holding the I Ching and press the read-tome key; interact tosses three coins, six times, bottom line first (heads 3, tails 2: 6 old yin and 9 old yang change, 7 young yang, 8 young yin). Then the hexagram, its changing lines and, if any change, the changed hexagram, with their readings. Reflection only: nothing in the world changes. trigram_order and king_wen give the number from the lower and upper trigrams (each trigram's lines bottom to top, 1 yang).

iching._help_king_wen: Rows: the upper trigram, columns: the lower, both in trigram_order.
iching.log_open: You set three coins on the log beside you.
